title: Virtual network fault-injection VCR harness for multi-SDK streaming contract tests
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a deterministic VCR-style test harness that can run contract tests across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs while simulating realistic network faults and timing nondeterminism for streaming endpoints. The goal is to catch regressions in retry/backpressure/streaming ergonomics and ensure contract compatibility for both chunked streaming and event/structured outputs. This harness should: 1) record live interactions with Redwood hosted test endpoints (with token scrubbing), 2) allow replay under controlled timing (latency/jitter, dropped chunks, half-close), and 3) validate SDK behavior against a pluggable contract assertion layer (order of events, retry semantics, idempotency of resumed streams). Re-use existing record/replay infra where it fits but add a virtual network layer and deterministic time control so CI runs are reproducible across platforms.
acceptance_criteria: A VCR recorder that captures streaming frames and connection-level events with scrubbed sensitive fields (API keys, timestamps) exists
A replay harness that can inject latency, jitter, chunk drops, and connection resets deterministically from a fixture file
Three example contract tests (Python, TypeScript, Go) validate streaming retry, resume, and correct ordering for a canonical streaming use-case
CI job executes the replayed tests on each PR and fails on contract assertion mismatches
Performance overhead of harness in CI is under 30% compared to current unit test runtime baseline
Documentation and a short how-to guide for writing new fixtures and assertions are merged into docs repo
tasks: Design network fault model and YAML fixture schema
Extend existing record-replay service to capture connection events and chunk metadata
Implement deterministic time controller library used for replaying fixtures
Add virtual network layer that enforces latency/jitter/drop schedules on replays
Create contract assertion DSL for streaming semantics (order, idempotency, resume tokens)
Write 3 cross-language example tests and CI job entries
Add scrubber to remove API keys, ephemeral timestamps, and noise from fixtures
Performance test the harness and iterate to meet CI runtime SLA

notes: This ticket intentionally focuses on cross-SDK deterministic replay for streaming. Separate follow-ups will target non-streaming VCRs, long-term fixture storage lifecycle, and access controls for raw recordings. The fixed-seed approach should aid debugging flakey tests by enabling exact reproduction locally.
qa_plan: Run the three cross-language contract tests in a canary CI pipeline for one week, collect flakes and file bugs. If flake rate > 0.5% open a follow-up to tighten timing granularity or adjust scrub rules.
risks: Differences in encoder buffering between SDKs may require adapter layers when comparing chunk-level fixtures. Large fixtures can bloat CI runtime and storage — we'll add fixture compaction and sampling if needed.
implementation_decisions: Use YAML for human-editable fixtures and gzipped JSONL for CI artifacts. Use deterministic pseudo-random generator with logged seed to drive drop schedules. Normalize chunk hashing to be encoding-agnostic by comparing decoded token sequences when available.
